**Summary of Medical Source Gathering for Week 10 (Days 64‑70)**

**What I did:**  
Performed targeted web searches for each of the four focus areas—infant social development, maternal return‑to‑work logistics, breastfeeding/pumping at work, and postpartum body image—to identify recent, peer‑reviewed or authoritative medical sources relevant to the approximately 10‑week postpartum period.

**What I found:**  
Below is a curated list of sources extracted from the search results (titles, URLs, and brief descriptions). These represent the most relevant medical/clinical information available via the search backend.

---

### 1. Infant Social Development (around 10 weeks)
- **Assessing and Improving Early Social Engagement in Infants – PMC**  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4193383/  
  Discusses baseline social engagement in early infancy, including eye contact and discriminative smiling at ~3 months.
- **Developmental Stages of Social Emotional Development in Children – StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf)**  
  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK534819/  
  Notes the first measurable social milestone: infants begin to smile socially in response to parental vocalizations/smiles around 1–2 months.
- **A Longitudinal Study of Maternal Postnatal Bonding and Psychosocial Factors that Contribute to Social‑Emotional Development**  
  https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10578-022-01398-5  
  Examines maternal bonding at 8 and 12 months postpartum and its association with child’s social‑emotional development; includes discussion of proximal stimulation (touching/kissing) at 12 weeks.
- **The influence of social support in the prevention and treatment of postpartum depression: An intervention‑based narrative review – PMC**  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11378223/  
  Reviews how maternal self‑confidence and social support affect infant care and development during the postpartum period.

### 2. Maternal Return‑to‑Work Logistics (around 10 weeks)
- **Work Reentry After Childbirth: Predictors of Self‑Rated Health in Month One Among a Sample of University Faculty and Staff – PMC**  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7078554/  
  Finds that >25% of U.S. women return to work within two months of giving birth; discusses predictors of health after return.
- **Returning to work after maternity leave – Mayo Clinic Health System**  
  https://www.mayoclinichealthsystem.org/hometown-health/speaking-of-health/returning-to-work-after-maternity-leave  
  Advises touching base with employer a few weeks before return to plan for pumping space and schedule.
- **Going back to work after baby: Timelines and tips – BabyCenter**  
  https://www.babycenter.com/baby/postpartum-health/when-can-i-go-back-to-work-after-delivery_1156149  
  Notes variability in return‑to‑work timing; some mothers return as early as a few weeks postpartum.
- **Returning to Work – 4th Trimester Project**  
  https://newmomhealth.com/selfcare/returning-to-work/  
  Suggests starting mid‑week can ease transition; provides practical tips for planning.

### 3. Breastfeeding and Pumping at Work (around 10 weeks)
- **Breastfeeding and going back to work – Office on Women's Health**  
  https://womenshealth.gov/breastfeeding/breastfeeding-home-work-and-public/breastfeeding-and-going-back-work  
  Recommends practicing milk expression by hand or pump several days/weeks before returning to work.
- **5 Tips for Returning to Work and Breastfeeding – CDC**  
  https://www.cdc.gov/breastfeeding/features/returning-to-work-and-breastfeeding.html  
  Suggests starting to pump a few weeks before return to help baby adapt to bottle feeding and build a freezer stash.
- **Pumping at Work: Example Schedule and Helpful Tips – Cleveland Clinic**  
  https://health.clevelandclinic.org/pumping-schedule-pumping-at-work  
  Indicates pumping every 3 hours is a typical goal for maintaining supply.
- **FLSA Protections to Pump at Work – U.S. Department of Labor**  
  https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/pump-at-work  
  Outlines federal rights: reasonable break time and a private, non‑bathroom space for expressing milk for up to 1 year postpartum.
- **Going Back to Work: A Pumping FAQ – Ingrid & Isabel**  
  https://www.ingridandisabel.com/blogs/mom-life/faq-guide-for-pumping-going-back-to-work  
  Advises starting to pump once a day after the first morning feed about one month before returning to work (avoid pumping in first 6 weeks to protect supply).

### 4. Postpartum Body Image (around 10 weeks)
- **Body image: a cross‑sectional study of the perception and practices of women after delivery – PMC**  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12486634/  
  Survey of postpartum women on body image perception, satisfaction, and practices to achieve ideal body after delivery.
- **Predictors of body image during the first year postpartum: a prospective study – PubMed**  
  https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/17613464/  
  Longitudinal study (N=79) tracking body image at 6 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months postpartum; examines feeling fat, attractiveness, salience of shape/weight, and strength/fitness.
- **A prospective study on body image disturbances during pregnancy and postpartum: the role of cognitive reappraisal – Frontiers in Psychology**  
  https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2023.1200819/full  
  Investigates changes in body image disturbance from prepartum to postpartum and the moderating role of cognitive reappraisal.
- **Improving body image and sexual life among postpartum women: a single‑blind randomized controlled trial – PMC**  
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9683934/  
  Evaluates a WhatsApp‑based CBT intervention for postpartum body image and sexual quality of life (82 women, 8 sessions over 2 weeks).
